title: ops-reliability-orchestra-sprint-canvas-2026-q2
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint canvas to orchestrate a 6-sprint initiative (12 weeks) to improve service dependability across high-throughput endpoints and put formal SLOs, error-budget workflows, and cross-team runbooks into day-to-day operations. The emphasis is practical: instrument, measure, protect, and practice via regular canaries and fallbacks, not just definitions on paper.

Primary goals (outcomes):
- Define and publish SLOs for 6 canonical services (api-gateway, text-gen-v1, chat-router, embed-indexer, batch-async, cache-proxy).
- Implement automated measurement and dashboards (per-route p50/p95/p99, availability, errors, dependent-service latency).
- Create error-budget burn policies and simple automated mitigation hooks (traffic shaping, model downgrade, throttles).
- Run 4 cross-team incident drills and one SLA cutover rehearsal.
- Reduce p99 generation latency tail by 18% for text-gen-v1 under median load in the test cluster.

Scope & out-of-scope:
- In scope: instrumentation, SLO targets, alerting rules, burn policies, runbooks, and rollout plan for dedicated + hosted endpoints.
- Out of scope: large infra reprovisioning (reserved for next quarter), full on-prem packaging.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Eng-SRE (owners): Aisha Patel (lead), Markus Chen (monitoring), Sophie Rivera (runbooks).
- Serving Runtime: Diego Alvarez (latency work), Linh Vo (kv-cache), PR owner for runtime changes.
- Product-Hosted-API: Priya Nair (customer-facing SLOs, rollout comms).
- Observability: Tom Becker (dashboards), QE: Rina Shah (scenarios).
- Solutions Eng: Liaison for enterprise customers, plays in canary rehearsals.

Principles we will follow:
1) Start small: create SLOs for 6 services first. 2) Measure what we can change: prefer latency & success-rate slices by route. 3) Automate simple mitigations before complex choreography. 4) Make the error-budget visible to teams and product owners.

SLO proposals (draft):
- api-gateway: availability 99.95% (monthly), p95 latency < 120ms, error-rate < 0.5%
- text-gen-v1: success-rate 99.7% (generation complete w/o internal error), p99 latency < 1.2s for short inputs (<128 tokens)
- chat-router: availability 99.9%, p95 routing latency < 80ms, misroute < 0.1%
- embed-indexer: batch success-rate 99.5%, throughput SLA 10k batches/hr for provisioned capacity
- batch-async: job completion SLA 98% within 15m for standard jobs
- cache-proxy: hit-rate target 60% for steady-state workloads (measured across 24h window)
Notes: These are conversation starters — objective is to agree on ONE metric per service for error-budgeting.

Instrumentation & measurement tasks (parallel workstreams):
- Metrics: standardize metric names, add tags (team, service, route, model_variant). Owner: Markus. Jira: ENG-4362.
- Traces: add heavy-tail sampling for text-gen p99 traces (collect top 100 traces/day). Owner: Diego.
- Logs: structured errors with error_code + upstream_dependency fields. Owner: Sophie.
- Dashboards: per-SLO dashboard with burn-rate panel + 7/30/90d trends. Owner: Tom.

Alerting & burn policy (proposal):
- Alert on error-rate crossing threshold that implies 24h projected SLO miss (burn-rate 24h > 1).
- Pager thresholds reserved for severity-high only when burn-rate sustained > 3x for 30m.
- Non-pager comms: #reliability-slo Slack channel with automatic messages from metrics-bot.
- Auto-mitigations (gated): attach traffic-shaping play (drop non-critical routes to preserve core gen). Implementation ticket ENG-4395.

Runbooks & drills:
- Runbook template: symptoms, triage checklist, mitigation knobs (throttle, downgrade, fallback-to-cache, region-shift), postmortem checklist.
- Drills: 4 scheduled drills in weeks 3, 6, 9, 11 — each drill exercises different mitigation.
- Owners do post-drill retrospective and update runbook within 48h.

Rollout and canary plan:
- Canary stage 1: internal test-cluster traffic (2%), validate instrumentation and SLA metrics.
- Canary stage 2: canary customers (10% traffic) for two days, validate error-budget behavior and automitigation.
- Safe rollout: 10% increments every 12h with rollback on burn-rate trigger.

Sprint plan (12 weeks, 6 sprints):
- Sprint 0 (week 0): kickoff, finalize SLO definitions, ownership sign-off, instrumentation spikes.
- Sprint 1 (weeks 1-2): metric naming, dashboards base, p95 panels, sample alerts.
- Sprint 2 (weeks 3-4): implement p99 tracing, runbook first drafts, first drill.
- Sprint 3 (weeks 5-6): build burn-rate automation (alerts -> channel + code hook), canary automation.
- Sprint 4 (weeks 7-8): mitigation implementations (throttle, downgrade), second & third drills.
- Sprint 5 (weeks 9-10): rollout rehearsals with product, finalize docs and handoff.
- Buffer & Cutover (weeks 11-12): enterprise communication, SLA notice, retro and open action list.

Dependencies & blockers:
- Observability infra capacity for p99 tracing (may need temporary storage bump). Owner: Tom. Risk: medium.
- Model variant metric tagging requires serving-runtime change. Owner: Diego. Risk: high.
- Legal/enterprise communication for any customer-visible SLA language. Owner: Priya. Risk: low.

Risk mitigation & contingency:
- If tracing storage unavailable: fallback to statistical sampling + synthetic replay.
- If model tagging late: instrument at gateway level as stopgap to classify by route + model header.

Communication cadence:
- Weekly sync: eng-sre + serving-runtime + product (30m) — Mondays 10:00.
- Drill retro: immediately after drill (1h).
- Weekly async update in confluence + summary thread in #reliability-slo Slack.

Acceptance criteria (done definition):
- SLO definitions published with owner sign-off in confluence.
- Dashboards live with correct metric names and automated burn calculation.
- At least 2 mitigations exercised successfully during drills.
- One customer-facing SLA draft reviewed by legal + product.

Open questions (needs decisions):
- Final SLA wording for hosted customers (Priya + Legal) — due by week 6.
- Pager escalation policy: do we keep burn-rate->pager mapping or only strict availability events? (ops leadership).
- Which mitigation knobs are approved for automated execution? (security/ops).

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Aisha: run kickoff with stakeholders and create JIRA epic ENG-4362 (done).
- Markus: publish metric naming doc draft (due Wed).
- Diego: spike to add model_variant tag at gateway (POC due Fri).
- Tom: estimate tracing storage delta and cost (due Fri).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep team-level burden low; prefer thin automation that surfaces decisions rather than auto-fixing everything.
- Document should become the source for SLO ownership boards.
- Expect follow-ups from solutions eng — reserve one drill slot for enterprise scenarios.

Attachments & references:
- Link to SLO template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/SLO+Template
- Existing incident runbook bucket: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Runbooks

Version history:
- 2026-03-04 created initial canvas (Aisha).
- 2026-03-10 updated alerts proposal after meeting with Tom (Markus).
- 2026-03-18 added sprint cadence and open questions (Aisha).

TODO (backlog):

- Add postmortem template linking to change window IDs.
- Authorize one mitigation for automated throttling (security sign-off).

End of working canvas.
